results.title: Delivering the Facts: Recycling Pizza Boxes
results.description: Domino’s customers throughout the U.S. may notice new pizza boxes featuring various recycling messages, delivered to their door beginning Aug. 22, 2022. Nearly everything that leaves a Domino’s store is in the same type of packaging: corrugated cardboard boxes.
snippets: These boxes are made of more than 70% recycled content. To continue to meet the demands for recycled content in corrugated packaging, Domino’s knows it is essential to spread awareness of pizza boxes’ recyclability.

However, an industry-endorsed study found that grease and cheese residue at typical levels did not have a significant impact on recyclability of pizza boxes. In reality, the majority of recycling programs and paper mills accept them without any problems. The American Forest & Paper Association, which represents 94% of the consumption of original corrugated containers, endorsed the study and subsequently issued new industry guidance that pizza boxes are indeed recyclable and not impacted by grease.

“Domino’s has advocated for pizza box recycling through recycling.dominos.com, customer emails, social media content and presentations to the American Pizza Community since 2020, during which we asked our peers to also promote the recyclability of pizza boxes,” Jenny said. “Domino’s is dedicated to not only diverting waste through responsible packaging, but through the recycling of that packaging.

The updated boxes note their recycled content and explain how to recycle them (it’s easy – eat, empty and place in bin!). Domino’s new boxes also feature a QR code which sends customers to recycling.dominos.com where they can read the facts and find their local pizza box recycling guidelines.

results.title: Domino’s Rebrand Debuts Bold Logo, Boxes & New Jingle
results.description: Domino’s unveils a bold rebrand with brighter colors, a new logo and font, black-and-gold premium boxes, and a Shaboozey “Dommmino’s” jingle rolling out now.
snippets: The pizza chain is updating its packaging with brighter colors, a new logo, a custom font, and redesigned boxes. Early fan reaction online is largely positive. Domino’s is flipping the whole look of the brand for the first time in 13 years. The pizza giant is rolling out a refreshed identity: brighter reds and blues, a thicker, “doughier” custom typeface, redesigned boxes, new uniforms, and a catchy audio twist.

The biggest visual shift is the packaging you’ll likely spot from across the living room. Core pies land in bold red or blue boxes with the domino mark dialed all the way up, while more premium bakes—think Handmade Pan and Parmesan Stuffed Crust—get dressed in black with metallic accents for a “treat-yourself” moment. “Give a raise to whoever turned the domino tiles into a box,” one fan said.

The company says the refresh is about staying modern for the next wave of pizza lovers, not patching holes. ... “Most companies rebrand themselves when they’re struggling, but after years of category-defying growth, this refresh is about continuing to push to be the best version of ourselves,” said Kate Trumbull, Domino’s executive vice president and global CMO, in a press release. Based on early comments, the crowd seems into it: “What’s this? A brand redesign that actually goes hard?” Another fan put it simpler: “I’ll literally buy Domino’s for doing a good modern rebrand.” And that’s kind of the whole point—Dom-mmm-ino’s wants you craving round two.
It's well worth the 13-year wait.

results.title: Unboxing the facts - Pizza Box Recycling
results.description: Empty, corrugated pizza boxes ARE recyclable...help us spread the word!
snippets: Recycling pizza boxes is an easy way to help reduce this number while providing the paper industry important and valuable fiber. ... In 2020, Domino’s increased its percentage of recycled content from 40% to 72. Most Domino’s products leave the stores in one type of packaging – corrugated boxes.

Pizza boxes are technically recyclable. They are made from the same material as a corrugated box, which has an average recovery rate for recycling of 92%. However, in the past, some paper mills and others in the recycling industry have expressed concerns about accepting them because of fear of food contamination.
AF&PA member companies representing 94 percent of the total annual U.S. old corrugated containers (OCC) consumption accept pizza boxes.- AF&PA
There are approximately 3 billion pizza boxes used in the U.S., annually, which represents 600,000 tons of highly desired corrugated material that should be recycled and not needlessly wasted.
